_description: Real-card GPU FFN-stage utilization for decode (batch=1). Used by rubin_ffn_decode.py to derate the Rubin FFN roofline: t_mem = bytes/(peak_BW*mem_util), t_compute = flops/(peak*compute_util). Same methodology as h100_rubin_utilization.json (attention side): GPU kernel efficiency is assumed to transfer across GPU generations (H100 -> Rubin).
_peak_ref: H100 SXM: HBM3 3350 GB/s, FP8 Tensor Core 1979 TFLOPS

_metrics.mem_util: achieved HBM read BW / peak (ncu HBM-BW% equivalent)

_caveats: DENSE numbers: ncu-MEASURED on real H100 (single_gpu_decode.ncu-rep, Qwen3-235B dense MLP inter=14336, fp16, decode b=1, seq-independent, MEM-bound).

MoE numbers: MEASURED on H100 GPU0 (2026-06-07) via profiling/microbench/microbench_moe_util.py (FP8, CUDA-graph + 16-distinct-weight pool to defeat L2/launch overhead), calibrated to ncu by /0.87 (the graph-vs-ncu ratio validated on the dense shape: graph 72.0%/66.5% vs ncu 82%/77%). Per-model because util depends on per-expert weight size.

Key result: MoE expert GEMVs realize FAR lower HBM util than the dense MLP -- qwen3 expert ~43%/28%, deepseek3 ~66%/48% vs dense 82%/77% -- because the per-expert weight (6-29MB) is too small to saturate HBM. The earlier dense-proxy was ~2x optimistic.
dtype: dense measured at fp16, MoE at fp8. Applied as an efficiency ratio to FP8 Rubin modeling (bytes counted at FP8).

moe_by_model._source: microbench_moe_util.py CUDA-graph on H100 GPU0, fp8, /0.87 ncu-calibrated

moe._source: generic fallback (deepseek3 measured) for models without moe_by_model entry
